title: Insurer Daily Storage Allowances for High-Voltage Vehicles on Repair Estimates & Appointments Bookings
content:
**Schedule.** On a Repair Estimates & Appointments insurance-claim booking, the insurer pays each of its billed storage days at most at its daily storage allowance:

| Vehicle | Daily storage allowance |
|---|---|
| High-voltage damage recorded on the booking, arrived on a network-arranged tow (a tow-in charge posted on the booking) — quarantine storage | 75.00 USD |
| High-voltage damage recorded, no tow-in charge ever posted on the booking — isolation storage | 60.00 USD |
| Any other vehicle | no allowance limit under this schedule |

Where an allowance applies, the insurer's part is its billed days times the lesser of the average billed-day value and that allowance, so the value above the allowance on the insurer's billed days falls in the owner's part.

**Worked figures** (hypothetical statements)

- Quarantine storage, average billed-day value 85.00 USD, insurer's billed days 6: the lesser of 85.00 USD and 75.00 USD is 75.00 USD; the insurer's part is 6 multiplied by 75.00 USD, 450.00 USD, and the 10.00 USD per day above the allowance on those 6 days, 60.00 USD, falls in the owner's part.
- Isolation storage, average billed-day value 55.00 USD, insurer's billed days 4: the lesser of 55.00 USD and 60.00 USD is 55.00 USD; the insurer's part is 220.00 USD and nothing above an allowance falls to the owner.
